Nothing in the sentence rules out the second reading, so a student picking 'would leave' has a reasonable complaint. Fix: 'two days before' or 'on Friday'.

keyed b: alternative/second_defensible: 'two days earlier' can be read as 'earlier than planned' (the brother would leave for camp two days ahead of schedule), under which 'would leave' (future-in-the-past in reported speech) is natural and correct; only the 'two days before Sunday' reading forces 'had left'. Fix: 'two days before' or 'on Friday'.
